memo.verdict: Bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction working hypothesis (medium-low). The record recommends progressing the case now rather than parking it, because the destocking concern is probably clearing, the odds on the cleared multiple are near even, and at 95.46 EUR (2026-09-17) the modal path pays the framework's 20 percent bar over eighteen months (about 20.6 percent a year) with a bounded downside (about -7 to -20 percent to the trough multiples on unchanged earnings). It does not pay the bar over three years (about 15.1 percent a year); below about 84 EUR it clears at both horizons; the eighteen-month clearing price is about 96 EUR. The conviction is low because the return meets the bar at eighteen months only on a blended multiple of 16.0x at 52 to 48 odds and the clearing evidence is one pricing-assisted quarter old. The first test is the nine-month results on 5 November 2026. Invalidation triggers named by the record: nine-month organic gross profit growth below 0 percent, or a group gross margin below 24.5 percent, or a conversion margin below 42 percent in H2 2026, any one of which moves the view to neutral and park. On a plausibly worse drop-through from EBITDA to cash EPS (FY2028 cash EPS 6.78 EUR rather than 7.10 EUR), the eighteen-month return falls to 16.9 percent a year, the ratings stay unchanged, and the recommendation would be neutral at this price (it would clear over eighteen months at about 88 EUR). The gate line does not apply: no D or F sits on management (B), business quality (B), predictability (C) or trackability (C).
case: IMCD is a good business coming out of a three-year earnings trough, and the trough is clearing for a cyclical reason, the end of destocking, that its foundations did not cause. At 95.46 EUR the shares pay the framework's 20 percent bar over eighteen months only if a partial re-rating is credited at near-even odds, and they do not pay it over three years. The whole case turns on whether organic gross profit growth stays positive as the Middle East pricing spike of 2026 unwinds.

The change is external and cyclical, and it has turned. The post-pandemic destocking cycle of 2024 and 2025 has ended. Organic gross profit, the line IMCD earns on, went from -7.2 percent in Q4 2025 to -3.7 percent in Q1 2026 to +7.3 percent in Q2 2026; organic revenue from -2.8 to -0.8 to +7.4 percent (consensus 5.2 percent). The turn is sector-wide: Azelis printed organic gross profit of +7.2 percent in the same quarter; customer inventories are lean and buying is just-in-time on a six-to-eight-week order book. Part of the Q2 growth was price passed through from the Middle East supply disruption that began in late February 2026 (Brent above 100 USD a barrel; container freight two to three times normal), and that pricing is already reversing: European ethylene fell 12.9 percent and propylene 14.2 percent in July 2026. How much was volume is not disclosed; that is the gap in the evidence. Management reports a promising, stable start to Q3 2026.

The internal change is continuity, not change. A 26-year insider replaced an abruptly departed chief executive on 24 April 2025 without a strategic pivot; the six pillars of the 2024 Milan investor day stand. The one internal force reaching the outputs is cost discipline: organic operating expenses were flat year on year in H1 2026 after a late-2025 restructuring, and the CFO says the cost base can take significantly higher volumes without a proportional headcount increase. The Q2 2026 conversion margin of 44.9 percent beat consensus of 43.1 percent by 183 basis points. There is no guidance to raise because the company gives none; acquisitions run at about a fifth of the 2025 pace (about 70 EURm of annualised revenue in H1 2026 against about 320 EURm added in 2025, seven deals for 437.2 EURm); the dividend was cut 16 percent for FY2025; buybacks are mooted, not begun. The framework's screen rule for internal change (three forces strong, or chief-executive change plus a guidance increase) is not met, so 'Internal forces' is C, 'Guidance raised' F, 'Strategy change' D, 'Shareholder returns' D, 'Standards improvement' B.
counter_case: At Building Block 1, the strongest case against is that the whole recovery is inflation, not volume, and it is already reversing. The Q2 2026 acceleration was price and pre-buying from the Strait of Hormuz disruption: Brent above 100 USD a barrel from late February 2026, container freight two to three times normal, principals' price increases of single digits to 40 percent passed straight through. Jefferies' own title for the quarter is inflation-driven. Azelis printed the identical organic gross profit growth of 7.2 percent, so nothing company-specific was proved. European petrochemical prices fell 12.9 to 14.2 percent in July 2026, so the tailwind is turning into a headwind now, and Deutsche Bank warns that if tensions ease and oil drops, gross margins fall back to pre-conflict levels and the premium multiple de-rates. Underneath, volumes are structurally weak in the Americas (organic revenue +1.6 percent in Q2 2026; organic EBITA -25 percent in Q1 2026; EBITA margin 8.8 percent) and in the semi-specialty fifth of revenue under Chinese pressure, where Chinese specialty pricing is 10 to 50 percent below Western peers and Morgan Stanley holds that increased Chinese supply continues to pressure volumes and pricing. Exclusivity terms are shortening from five-year commitments to twelve-month reviews. The 91.4 percent cash conversion of FY2025 is a counter-cyclical working-capital release that must reverse; net working capital is already 24.5 percent of revenue at H1 2026 against 21.6 percent, and broker research expects conversion to fall to the mid-80s. The acquisition engine is throttled at 2.8x leverage. So H2 2026 organic gross profit turns negative, estimates are cut a fourth year, and the multiple, still a 32 percent premium to peers on EV/EBITDA, goes to 13x or below, toward the sell-side's downside of 70 EUR, a fall of 27 percent, or 60 EUR (-37 percent) on a 10x EV/EBITA multiple and an 8.5 percent EBITA margin. IMCD does not disclose volumes, so this cannot be disproved from the accounts, and management itself declines to split volume from price. The record concedes: the Q2 print was pricing-assisted; the durability of organic gross profit growth is unproven and is the whole bet; the Americas is a real problem; cash conversion will fall; on the uncleared branch with earnings also cut the downside is 20 to 30 percent and no separable asset bounds it. The record's odds on this hypothesis are the 48 percent of the uncleared branch, on which, at 14.5x, the eighteen-month return is still 13.1 percent a year on the record's earnings and negative only if earnings are also cut. The record's answer: the case does not need the price rises to last, because sector-wide destocking has demonstrably ended and the ten-year organic rate of 6 to 7 percent resumed as soon as it did; EMEA organic revenue of +10.3 percent against Azelis' +0.4 percent is share gain from supplier mandates that inflation does not explain; organic costs are flat, so even 4 percent organic gross profit growth delivers EBITA growth of 8 to 10 percent; specialty price rises were low single digits, so the give-back is small; and the multiple at the 19th percentile of five years already discounts a non-recovery. The counter-case wins if volumes are still falling underneath the price cover, which the nine-month results on 5 November 2026 show.

At Building Block 2, the case against is that the moat is a marketing story: laboratories are a baseline staffed by one or two people; customers prioritise availability and response time over technical service and split orders among Azelis, Brenntag and IMCD; customer contracts are one year or less with pricing commitments of six months; exclusivity is narrowing by geography and category; return on invested capital has halved from 16.9 percent in 2022 to 10.4 percent; a competitor's executive says the core business is loss-making organically excluding acquisitions; a former Azelis COO calls the customised ERP a dinosaur; a former India general manager describes ERP-driven inventory damage and supplier write-offs; net working capital is 68 days against Azelis' 51. The record concedes the moat is a formulation moat, not a general one, holding only on the customised specialty share, and that the returns are those of a good distributor. It answers that the ten-year organic gross profit growth of 6 to 7 percent a year, the 91.4 percent cash conversion, the EMEA share gain against Azelis, and principals cutting the sales staff a bypass would need are outputs a marketing story cannot produce. What would change its mind: a group gross margin below the 21 to 24 percent normalised range, or exclusivity coverage reported below 90 percent.
triggers: - The decisive test: the nine-month results on 5 November 2026. Organic gross profit growth still positive with the group gross margin at or above 24.5 percent confirms the case, lifts 'Clearing evidence' and the 'Investment Setup' to B, and Headline Rating 4 to B. Nine-month organic gross profit growth below 0 percent, or a gross margin below 24.5 percent, or a conversion margin below 42 percent in H2 2026 moves the view to neutral and park; the Building Block 1 invalidation is nine-month organic gross profit growth below 0 percent with a gross margin below 24.5 percent.

- Invalidate levels in the monitoring table: organic gross profit growth below 0 percent for two consecutive quarters or below -4 percent in one; conversion margin below 40 percent; gross margin below 24.0 percent; APAC organic gross profit negative for two quarters; an Americas conversion margin below 40 percent; exclusivity coverage reported below 90 percent. Alarm levels: organic gross profit growth below +2 percent in any quarter; conversion margin below 42 percent; the 24-month-forward multiple below 13.87x; gross margin below 24.5 percent; double-digit growth in Chinese specialty exports; acquired revenue below 100 EURm in a year; leverage above 3.0x excluding acquisitions; Americas organic growth below 0 percent; net working capital days above 70; any three-month consensus cut; senior regretted attrition above 6 percent; the order book shortening below six weeks; organic cost growth above gross profit growth in a half.
- The unresolved evidence gap: IMCD does not disclose volume against price, so the pricing-versus-volume question cannot be settled from the accounts; the second half of 2026 settles it.

- 'Margin' in 'Key metrics' becomes B on a second quarter of conversion margin above 44 percent. 'Goldilocks growth' becomes B if the conversion margin returns to the 45 to 46 percent normal, adding about 3 points a year to the three-year rate.

- The stale earnings-momentum pin: re-run on September data it would read C or B; the pin stays F until re-pinned. Even with 'Clearing evidence' at B and the pin at C, 'No broad mediocrity' stays capped at D (B 20 and C 18 of 39); three attributes moving from C to B are needed to reach a C.
- The 'Compounder' question: whether the acquisition engine is throttled or stalled; a year below 100 EURm of acquired revenue with leverage above 2.5x says stalled.

judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** M. Materials. Industry RS 59 at the Friday 2 October reading (59 four weeks earlier)
- **Sector:** M.2. Chemicals, distributors. Sector RS 81 at the 30 September month-end (85 four weeks earlier; 53 twelve weeks earlier). Its other companies: Azelis (Stock RS 78, in the Pool), Brenntag (65)
- **Cohort:** specialty chemical distributors. The cohort's relative strength 77 (81 four weeks earlier), 4 companies: Azelis (78, in the Pool), DKSH (75), Brenntag (65)


**What is going on, and why it matters**

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock fell 0.5% to EUR 95.72; the market's fall explains all of it, so its own move was nil. Over 20 sessions it fell 1.1%, an own move of +0.4%, nothing against its usual size. No public news; nothing is happening in the price
- **The sector and cohort:** the sector (81) and cohort (77) are strong and Azelis is in the Pool: the end of destocking is being priced across the distributors. IMCD's own Stock RS is 67 at the month-end (73 at the end of August), just below the 70 line of the third criterion, information only
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates +43% and target prices +47% (57% and 47% at the end of August): analysts raising on both counts; Sell-side Momentum B, from F

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** a Probing Bet, so its 20-day moving-average stop at EUR 94.04 governs: the price is about 2% above it, but the exit was confirmed on 21 September (the five-day rule, volume not light) and a confirmed exit stays confirmed when the price recrosses the stop. The rule's answer is sell at this session (decision 1)
- **Selling:** at this session. If you keep one of the three, this is the one: the price is back above the stop, the memo is bullish, the sector is strong and the 20-day stop is the tightest in the book; a keep is recorded as an overrule with your reason
- **Adding:** not allowed while the confirmed exit stands

**What we could lose:** about 0.04% of the fund's capital, to the stop; 0.33% to the relative 52W high trigger and 0.54% to the 30% level, information only

**Experiment: which stocks IMCD's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)

- **Brenntag** (same sector and cohort): 0.70 and 0.70, strong
- **Azelis** (same sector and cohort): 0.54 and 0.61, strong
- **DKSH** (same cohort): 0.28 and 0.28, weak
- **Heineken** (same country of listing): 0.32 and 0.10, weak
- **My reading:** look at Brenntag first; the two distributors are one trade

**The Investment Analyst's memo (digest of 18 September at EUR 95.46; memo republished 1 October)**

- **Decided:** bullish; progress to Early-Stage; conviction a working hypothesis (medium-low); gates management B, business quality B, predictability C, trackability C
- **Must happen:** nine-month organic gross profit growth still positive with the group gross margin at or above 24.5% at the 5 November results; a partial re-rating at near-even odds
- **Main risk:** the recovery is inflation and pre-buying rather than volume, and already reversing; a conversion margin below 42% in the second half
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** about 20.6% a year over eighteen months at EUR 95.46, meeting our bar; 15.1% a year over three years; clears both below about EUR 84
- **Next test:** the nine-month results on 5 November

**My judgement:** neutral on the position, medium conviction: the rule sells it today and I would follow the rule, because the rule's value is that it is followed, and a 20-day stop confirmed and then recrossed is noise in both directions, so nothing in the price argues for an exception

- Of the three sales it is the one to keep if you keep any, and the one most likely to return as a Core Investment through the Pool once its Stock RS passes 80.
- **Counter-case:** selling, 2% above a 20-day average, a stock whose memo meets our bar, whose analysts are raising and whose sector reads 81 is the rule at its most mechanical; the decisive test is four weeks away and the price is going nowhere in the meantime

**What would change my view:** the 5 November results (organic gross profit growth; the 24.5% gross margin); a Stock RS above 80 at a month-end, which would make it a Pool name; a close below EUR 94.04 again
